geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
Practice the lessons so far, then check your answers.

Goal: I can find volumes of solids.

  • 12.1 I can describe relationships of lines and planes in space.
  • 12.2 I can identify nets and cross sections of solids.
  • 12.3 I can explain why two solids between the same two parallel planes with equal cross-sectional areas at every height have equal volume.
  • 12.4 I can derive V = Bh from unit cubes and Cavalieri.
  • 12.5 I can explain why V = (1/3)Bh.
  • 12.6 I can use Cavalieri to relate a hemisphere to a cylinder minus a cone.
  • 12.8 I can find surface area of prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, and spheres.
  • 12.9 I can solve volume and surface area problems with composite solids and variables.
  • 12.10 I can use k, k^2, k^3 for lengths, areas, and volumes.
  • 12.11 I can identify the five Platonic solids and test Euler's formula.
  • 12.12 I can use geometric methods to design an object meeting constraints.
  • 12.14 I can describe how triangles on a sphere break Euclid's angle sum. (Enrichment, non-Euclidean.)

slides.title: Practice: 12.1
slides.html: Can two lines that never meet fail to be parallel?
slides.reveal: Yes, in space: skew lines never meet and are not parallel because they are not in one plane.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • volume and surface area scale by the same factor
  • a cone is half a cylinder
  • slant height equals height
  • Cavalieri needs identical cross-section shapes (only equal areas are needed)
